rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest call: chunk 20 "/goal", line 328, "The runtime-shipped sibling of the verifier you author later in the training" — "the verifier" is never named earlier in the file, a forward reference by rule-1's literal text. Stays inside: the clause is trailing apposition after /goal's full definition in the same paragraph; a reader who cannot place "the verifier" yet loses nothing about what /goal itself does. Second candidate checked: chunk 37 line 561's "Ralph re-feed verifier" and chunk 17 line 312's "Ralph-style re-feed" — "Ralph" is never defined in this file, but the file's own "Related AE101 modules" map (chunk 42) ties §17/§20 to M6 ("Ralph→/goal story"), i.e. arc-earned spine vocabulary earned in M6's body before a student reaches this page's Long-running-shapes sections — the carve-out this file already leans on elsewhere for "un-packaged send-off" and "packaging." No unresolved referent found on a sequential read of all 43 chunks.

Only cross-file callback that isn't a plain "AE101 cross-refs:" module-name pointer: chunk 34 line 480, "The closing lecture on packaging names that property 'hooks always fire.'" — named by topic ("on packaging") and unpacked by its exact claim in the same sentence, not by position ("the last lecture"), matching the compendium's own PASS example shape. Confirmed the source exists and carries that framing: `curriculum/lectures/what-packaging-is.md` is on disk and this file's own chunk 37 (line 566) independently names it as "M5 closer lecture (`what-packaging-is.md`)". No "the opening lecture said…"-style bare positional pointer anywhere in the body.

Not [A-Za-z].*\.'` → 0), zero self-grading superlatives (`grep -niE 'one of the (most|best)|most useful|extremely|incredibly|game.?chang'` → 0), zero number+retraction pairs (`grep -niE 'could be more|about [0-9]+%'` → 0). rules_evaluated.evidence: `grep -niE 'compendium|forcing function|\bbeat\b|\bmood\b|Connections\b'` on the body → 0 hits. rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Emphasis budget — bold is for handles, and go very lightly.
rules_evaluated.evidence: This is a lookup surface ("Flat look-up for the primitives AE101 leans on", line 3), so §9's per-slide bold-COUNT budget is off by its own reference/supplementary-page waiver. The remaining handle-cap sub-clause ("bold the label, not the sentence after it") is genuinely in tension here: counted words on ~13 bolded leads across chunks 2, 6, 7, 8, 10, 13, 14, 15, 18, 23, 33, 34 run 6-13 words (e.g. chunk 18 line 318, "Tasks fire only while the app is open and the machine is awake" = 13 words; chunk 33 line 452, "CLAUDE.md is loaded as a user message, not the system prompt" = 11 words) — a strict reading would flag them. Checked for a counter-example inside the same file: chunk 31 ("/clear and /compact") bolds only the command name ("**`/clear`** starts a new conversation…") and leaves the claim plain, proving the compliant label-only shape is available and used elsewhere in this document — so the long bolds elsewhere are not simply unreachable. Harm test per dispatch-preamble: the bolded text IS the scannable payload a reader hunting for a specific fact needs ("Laptop sleep freezes the session", "Ctrl+C during a tool call can corrupt the session") — compressing to a bare topic label ("Laptop sleep") would remove the very fact the waiver's own rationale ("find the row that answers it") requires be scannable, unlike `/clear`/`/compact` where the label IS the fact (a command name). Not filed as REVISE: this is a rule question for the maintainer — what §9 would need to say to resolve it cleanly is that a lookup-page entry may bold a short CLAIM (not just a noun label) when the claim itself, not a proper noun standing in for it, is what a scanning reader searches for.
